page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.6xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 24 vCPUs (12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled) operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. For local storage, it bundles 15,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, designed for high-throughput, low-latency data access. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are included in this hardware profile.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory write operations, with large-block memory write bandwidth reaching 107.16 GB/sec. Single-core processing is highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 and strong text processing performance. Multi-core performance is also robust, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 16504.0 and a static web serving throughput of 45.64 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the CPU-based LLM inference achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 415.29 tokens/sec on a small 135M model.

Given the high density of both DDR5 memory and local NVMe SSD storage, the i7ie.6xlarge offers a highly resource-dense profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive local storage combined with substantial memory capacity, avoiding the latency of network-attached storage. This configuration is well-suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput transactional systems, data indexing, and memory-intensive caching layers.
